scope: Current first-party working tree: core replacements, retired inherited addons, native feature replacements, supporting tooling, documentation and translations. Earlier release archives and Git history are not relicensed.
implementationMethod: Public APIs, database schemas, stored formats and previous behavior were inspected to preserve compatibility. Replacement implementations were authored for Monolith; inherited addon packages and unused assets were retired. This was not a clean-room process. Exact/branding-normalized matching and line overlap were triage aids followed by source review, not proof of authorship or a legal clearance opinion.

licenseScope.appliesTo: Current first-party Monolith software, documentation and replacement translations under 0BSD.
licenseScope.exclusions: Third-party libraries, icons, fonts, exercise data and the directly sourced Tesseract model retain their own terms. Historical versions keep the licenses supplied with them. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

batches.description: Form defaults and field binding, file conversion, input shells, text/numeric/search controls, listboxes/comboboxes, color/icon/date/file pickers, tags/settings rows, feedback, pagination/tabs, virtual layout, view preferences, modal manager/header, button styling, sidebar navigation, verification/vault screens, QR scan lifecycle, scoped print themes, native checkbox/switch/range controls, tag entry, isolated background rendering, desktop/mobile sidebar preferences, font lifecycle, generated theme palettes, recurrence editing, location search, form-dialog submission, shared layout and typography primitives, responsive style resolution, query/encryption wrappers, cards, menus, confirmation dialogs, Storybook documentation and native scroll lifecycle.

Replaced logging, typed route/response definitions, database reference validation, contract generation, file metadata/storage providers and upload staging. Stored file identifiers, table columns and public module APIs remain compatible.

New request transport and error decoding, concurrent session refresh, sign-in and sign-out lifecycle, native/web helpers, socket recovery, mutation hooks, typed contract proxies and RSA-OAEP/AES-GCM wire encryption. Existing server routes, stored values and encrypted request formats remain compatible.

New server-side add-on discovery, serialized imports, registry ownership, schema restoration on package rollback, filesystem watcher, module alias resolution, database relation composition and scoped transactions. Client-side federation registration/loading, metadata providers and localization startup/loading are replaced.
New journal UI, category management, dashboard widget, validation, database access and API routes. Existing table names, primary keys, category relationships and difficulty values are preserved.

Replaced module metadata extraction, client/server Vite setup, theme compilation integration, development middleware and add-on aliases. All 19 add-on manifests produce the same metadata as the previous extractor.

Replaced browser sign-in, refresh rotation, sign-out, authenticator setup, QR claims, authentication middleware, account bootstrap/profile/media/preferences endpoints, locale catalog loading, socket-session lifecycle, credential checks, API-key lookup, app middleware assembly, notification startup and graceful shutdown. Public routes, stored identity formats and data tables are preserved.

Replaced provider composition, queued account preference persistence, API-key prerequisite screens, language initialization, browser route assembly, remote route loading, QR sign-in presentation, responsive dashboard controls and appearance settings including font catalog/upload management and image adjustments. Superseded components were backed up locally before retirement.

Replaced heartbeat persistence, coding metrics, activity calendars, project/language reports, dashboard widget, stats image rendering and translations. The existing daily activity table, API routes and minute/millisecond wire units are preserved. The inherited chart components and static statistics image template were retired.

Replaced focus session persistence and settings, deadline-based timer engine, account/server-scoped draft recovery, shared add-on provider, session library and editors, interval history and Actions-connected widget. Existing session IDs, plans, recorded intervals and uploaded notification sounds remain compatible. The inherited default bell asset and superseded components were retired.

Replaced collection and folder persistence, typed note/image/link entries, tag management, bounded link previews, gallery and editors, folder drag/drop, dashboard capture widget and four translations. Existing collection and entry identifiers, media keys, subtype tables and API shapes remain compatible. The previous provider, page tree, edit modals and recursive search implementation were retired.

Replaced task CRUD, completion and catalog persistence, date/status filtering, calendar event export, task and catalog editors, filters, deep links and dashboard widget. Existing task IDs, list/tag/priority references, notes and completion timestamps remain compatible. Four new translations replace inherited copy; the previous provider, task/sidebar components, edit modals and unused AI prompt constants were retired.

Replaced notebook, subject and entry persistence with owner-scoped operations, folder ancestry validation, optimistic revisions and canonical-content validation. Replaced generic CRUD panels with notebook-specific editors, attachment controls, navigation guards and four translations. Existing IDs, table definitions, file keys, deep links and document-link integration remain compatible.

Replaced owned deck, card and tag persistence, review scheduling, library editors, study rounds and dashboard widget. Stored IDs, review/correct counters, next-review timestamps and table relationships remain compatible. The inherited generic entity panels and duplicated client schemas were retired; all four locale files were authored anew.

Replaced locale consistency scanning and consolidated ESLint configuration assembly. Reimplemented hook spacing with comment/indentation/line-ending preservation. Retired superseded lint wrappers and the unused inherited OpenAI/Zod response-format helper.

Replaced CLI JSON persistence, add-on/locale release pins, dependency manifest editing and package-version bump/restore. Existing lockfile formats and fields are retained; writes use a temporary file and rename, malformed records are rejected and prototype-named keys are handled as data.

Removed all 12 inherited addon packages and their distribution entries. Calendar and Projects use the native workspace record implementations; Journal has a new native page and composer. Replaced the old-addon bridge with a native record/custom Agents queue adapter. Custom queue schemas preserve saved IDs without importing the retired Projects package. Removed Notes table dependencies from the canonical document service.

Replaced CLI command execution, service orchestration, source installation/publishing, transactional schema reconciliation, account bootstrap and shell components, API initialization/schema declarations, file and addon asset serving, diagnostics, browser bootstrap, guidance and retained long-form translation messages. Updated agent tools to native workspace/calendar routes. Replaced the inherited OCR model with a pinned Apache-2.0 source download.

checks.result: 220 tests passed across 54 files; UI and web-client TypeScript checks passed. Production UI and Storybook builds and browser checks passed, including native scrolling to content edges.

Five PostgreSQL-compatible PGlite tests and client/server TypeScript checks passed; production add-on CRUD, category filters, widget refresh and failed-save retry passed against the current production UI bundle.
Eight tests and TypeScript checks passed, including structured errors, stream reuse/reopen and flushing; production package build passed on the isolated Mac mini checkout.

Thirty tests and TypeScript checks passed, including PostgreSQL-compatible reference batching and constraint errors, cyclic schema handling, response contracts and generated file writes. Production package build passed.

Thirty-four tests and TypeScript checks passed, including interrupted/oversized uploads, multipart rejection, thumbnail generation, safe replacement, namespace boundaries and object-store pagination. SDK requests were simulated; no live S3 bucket was used.

81 tests passed across 21 files, plus TypeScript and production builds. Coverage includes request decoding, refresh concurrency and logout races, authentication, socket cleanup, independent Node-crypto checks of encrypted requests/responses, mutation invalidation and isolated query inputs.

23 tests passed across five files, including failed-package rollback, cached-schema restoration, invalidated manifests, client-only replacements, concurrent imports, unchanged timestamps, path boundaries and watcher lifecycle. TypeScript and production builds passed.

Seven replacement tests passed across two files, including real PGlite persisted relations, rejected transaction rollback, committed writes, scope changes and duplicate table rejection. TypeScript and production builds passed.

12 federation tests and five localization tests passed, with TypeScript and production builds. Browser integration with the rebuilt API/UI/Achievements add-on passed. Full server TypeScript and the 30 server-SDK / five Achievements database checks also passed against the rebuilt runtime and database packages.

Production build and Chromium checks passed: dropdown focus, keyboard tabs, 1,000-item virtual gallery, picker validation/cancel/commit, file upload failure/retry, verification keyboard submission, sidebar actions, native checkbox/switch keyboard input, precise and keyboard slider input, tag deduplication/IME composition, recurring-rule preservation/editing, location provider error/retry/search and dark/light responsive rendering. Theme generation check passed. QR camera lifecycle is tested with simulated scanner events; physical-camera scanning was not exercised.

82 checks across seven files, TypeScript and production build passed. Manifest output compared equal for all 19 add-ons. Production web and add-on fixture builds passed using the replacement configuration package.

58 checks across 13 files passed, including PGlite-backed authentication, account updates, refresh replay protection, MFA/QR claim races, middleware scoping, locale catalog isolation and socket-session cleanup. Full API TypeScript and production build passed. No production account or database was used.

75 web tests across 19 files passed. Full web TypeScript and production build passed. Production Chromium checks passed for preferences hydration, save failure restoration, font favorites, background adjustments, font-dialog validation and light/dark/mobile rendering. QR transport remains covered by the existing session tests; no physical QR scan was performed in this batch.

16 tests across four files, client/server TypeScript and production bundles passed. PGlite checks preserve stored IDs, reject duplicate minute counts, handle object-property names safely and roll back failed requests. Production browser checks passed for shared authentication/transport, history ranges, grouping, widget settings, failed-query retry, historical calendars and mobile layout.

15 tests across three files passed, including PGlite session compatibility, completion deduplication, transaction rollback, settings preservation and cascading deletion. Timer checks cover clock deadlines, pauses, long-break progression, suspended tabs, malformed drafts and account/server isolation. Client/server TypeScript and production bundles passed. Browser checks passed for shared provider/widget state, selected-session reload, legacy draft recovery, countdown and pause/resume, completion messages, linked Action completion, failed-save retry, session creation, settings and mobile layout. Audio playback hardware was not tested.

12 tests across two files, client/server TypeScript and production bundles passed. PGlite checks cover saved IDs and media keys, counts, ancestry and cycle rejection, cross-collection isolation, atomic subtype replacement, rollback, recursive search, tag-reference updates and cascading deletion. Preview checks reject private/reserved addresses and unsafe protocols and bound cache retention. Production browser checks passed for shared authentication and transport, collections, widget capture, link/image viewing, failed-save retry, tag renaming, drag/drop, editing, root moves, archive/restore, search and mobile layout. Browser transport and native media URLs used isolated fixtures.

Nine PGlite-backed tests passed for saved task compatibility, date-only and timed deadlines, time-zone and DST boundaries, literal text search, catalog counts and references, completion/reopen timestamps, rollback and calendar export. Client/server TypeScript and production bundles passed. Production browser checks passed for shared auth/transport, calendar deep links, saved dates, note edits, selectors, date-only creation, failed-save retry, failed-toggle recovery, completion and reopening, synchronized widget state, search, catalog creation/rename, widget filters and mobile layout. No production task data was changed.

Nine PGlite checks, client/server TypeScript and production builds passed. Checks cover retained records and media references, owner boundaries, folder cycles and moves, stale revisions, content validation, request rollback, attachment reference replacement/detach and cascades. Production Chromium checks passed for shared authentication, deep links, existing content, failed-save retry, unsaved navigation protection, stale-draft rejection after background refresh, attachment download links/detach, folder placement, notebook/subject creation, search and mobile layout. External object-store deletion rollback was not exercised.

Seven PGlite tests, client/server TypeScript and production bundles passed. Checks cover saved history, account boundaries, foreign-parent rejection, remembered/missed schedules, atomic concurrent review counts, transaction rollback, cascade/reference behavior and blank-answer rejection. Production browser checks passed for shared authentication and queries, creation retry, saved-card history, validation, widget deck selection, answer visibility per card, failed-review retry, updated counts, restart, read-only mode, widget management, search and mobile layout. Browser transport used an isolated fixture.

12 tests across two files and targeted TypeScript checks passed. Locale checks now report missing/extra files and invalid JSON explicitly; rule tests cover comments, indentation, member calls, multiline expressions, export boundaries and CRLF stability. Resolved rules, plugins, globals and parser options compare equal to the previous ESLint setup across app, server test, Storybook and CLI files. This is a configuration-equivalence check, not a claim that the entire repository is lint-clean.

Seven new persistence tests passed, alongside the existing three registry configuration and two add-on packaging checks. Full CLI TypeScript passed. Tests cover preserved metadata, both lock namespaces, release-pin mismatches, malformed-file recovery, version rollback, dependency editing, prototype keys and failed serialization without overwriting existing JSON.
All locale files and keys now match the English reference; missing plural keys added and unused inherited fetch-action strings removed.

138 native client tests and 30 isolated native API/shop tests pass, including Journal revisions and access control, native calendar occurrences, project/action relations with and without Agents, and retired catalog rejection. Client/API/custom-queue typechecks and core production bundles pass. Go gateway tests pass; its opt-in PostgreSQL integration suite was not enabled. No production data changed. Production Journal browser checks pass with isolated data: search/month filters, save failure/retry without duplicate databases, draft discard/navigation protection, viewer controls and desktop/mobile layout. The editor-opening handoff uses a test probe; native record editing is covered by API tests. Website production build, typecheck, 3,236 internal links/assets and seven Chromium checks pass.

CLI, API and web TypeScript pass. Eight CLI/package lifecycle tests, 136 enabled API tests, 77 web tests, and nine focused asset/catalog/media tests pass. Real isolated PostgreSQL checks cover full schema creation/repeat application, persisted data, rejected constraint migration rollback, additive migration and owner policies. Compiled API boots with a non-superuser role and returns healthy status and an encryption key. Official OCR model recognizes a rendered fixture. API and web production builds pass. Opt-in service integrations requiring configured providers were not enabled.

Production Chromium checks pass for first-account validation, failed-save draft retention, login, connection failure/retry and mobile width using an isolated API fixture. Website production build and typecheck pass; all 3,236 internal links/assets verify. Locale consistency and 29 first-party 0BSD metadata checks pass. Staged gitleaks scan reports no secrets. Provider-dependent integrations remain opt-in.

hashMethod: SHA-256 of UTF-8 text with CRLF normalized to LF; third-party binary hashes are explicitly identified separately.
